chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about wine in which something is made until it ferments/sours, and he said, 'If that which was made in it is dominant over what was made in it, there is no harm.'

Because this is a strange (shadh) report on which action is not permissible, for we have clarified that wine is impure and it impurifies anything placed in it, and it does not become pure by anything that dominates it in any state. Therefore, this is a rejected report, and that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: A strange/rare report (counter to established norms)

ai.seo_question: Does mixing other substances make wine pure if they dominate it?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi presents this isolated report (*khabar shadh*) from Abu Basir to illustrate a minority view where wine's impurity might be negated if a dominant substance is added. However, the scholar rejects this as *matruk* (abandoned), affirming the standard Shia position that wine (*khamr*) remains inherently impure (*najis*) and does not purify through mixture, regardless of the proportion of other ingredients.
